about: Heat-set insert pockets. The pocket is read from the B-rep of the printed body, from its mouth inwards: melt relief, lead-in, hole. Every insert in the model is the golden model of its kind, sits on the axis of a pocket of that kind and ends flush with the relief floor. All lengths in mm. A project changes a number only in its gate/settings.json ("heatset": {...}, merged over this file).

M3x4x5.about: brass M3 insert, 4.0 long, spiral knurl D5.0, smooth pilot band D4.2 (Printec TBSK style)

golden.name: Heat-set insert M3x4x5 (golden)
golden.source: decided 2026-11-23 from the table numbers (length 4.0, knurl D5.0, pilot band D4.2); the pilot length and the bore are drawn, not measured. The pilot band is the end that goes in first, so it points to the bottom of the pocket

M3x4x5.source: measured: coupon in PETG-CF on a Bambu P2S, X-Y hole compensation 0.125, cycloidal drive project, 2026-11-12 (D4.4 x 1.5 lead-in + D3.6 grips and goes in straight; straight D4.4 pulled out by hand; D3.4 too tight). Relief D7.5 x 0.54 (3 layers of 0.18) is an owner decision; D6.5 and D5.9 are the smaller reliefs where D7.5 does not fit

pocket_signature.about: A hole is read as an insert pocket when, from an open end inwards (past a wider recess), it has a lead-in diameter of a kind within 2 mm of the mouth, or a relief diameter of a kind followed by any segment. A hole with such a shape and no insert in it is a finding.
